heading: EXT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN CONCESSION ROOF - NIGHT

units.text: EXT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN CONCESSION ROOF - NIGHT
A flat tar roof ringed by rusted floodlights.
The screen beyond it stands bare, a white rectangle against a sky full of cricket noise.
Weeds crack the asphalt below.
ILSE VANTERPOOL, seventeen, sits on the parapet, boots dangling over a drop she does not look at.
She wears her brother's varsity jacket, sleeves rolled twice.
A cigarette burns down in her fingers, unsmoked.
RODRIGO ACOSTA, eighteen, lanky, a trombone case at his feet, climbs the last rung of the ladder and stops three steps away.
He holds a paper bag.
You said you'd be at the recital.
units.name: RODRIGO

units.text: I said I'd think about it.
units.name: ILSE

units.text: He sets the bag down.
He sits, not close, not far.
A moth batters the nearest dead lamp.
It went okay.
units.name: RODRIGO

units.text: Did you play the part?
units.name: ILSE

units.text: Which part?
units.name: RODRIGO

units.text: You know which part.
units.name: ILSE

units.text: He opens the case.
He doesn't take the instrument out.
He just lifts the lid, as though to let the night look in.
I skipped it.
units.name: RODRIGO

units.text: Why?
units.name: ILSE

units.text: Wasn't mine to play.
units.name: RODRIGO

units.text: She stubs the cigarette against the parapet, a long slow press.
Then she laughs, one dry breath, and her shoulders drop.
He passes her the bag.
She takes out a warm paper-wrapped churro, bites it, and holds the rest out to him without turning her head.
The screen glows, faintly, with starlight.
